title: What does the XRPL DisallowXRP account flag mean?
abstract: Sourced explanation of DisallowXRP and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, DisallowXRP is an advisory request that clients avoid sending XRP to the account; the protocol does not enforce it as a universal rejection. [1]

Do not use it as a security boundary for preventing deposits. Receiving applications can display the preference, but a sender may still submit XRP. DepositAuth serves a different purpose and has its own rules. Distinguish a client warning from an enforced ledger permission when explaining why a payment can succeed. [1][2]

XRPL distinguishes an AccountSet option from the AccountRoot bit that records the resulting state. SetFlag and ClearFlag use option identifiers, while the ledger Flags field stores bit values; the numbers are not interchangeable. Read the documented mapping for DisallowXRP and check the validated account state after any permitted change. A successful submission response alone does not establish that the requested state is final. [1][2]

Author interpretation: document why DisallowXRP is needed, who may authorize a change and what existing users would experience. Review irreversible settings before issuance and test reversible settings with representative counterparties. This is guidance for interpreting account controls, not a live network measurement. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
